claims.text: Post-deposition annealing reduces residual internal stresses in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons.
Post-deposition annealing reorders the microstructure and produces a more uniform grain or defect distribution.
Residual-stress relaxation and defect reduction decrease magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Reduced magnetic domain-wall pinning lowers magnetic hysteresis.
Reduced magnetic domain-wall pinning makes the magnetocaloric process more reversible.
Improved microstructural uniformity enhances local thermal pathways and heat transfer.
Enhanced local thermal pathways mitigate heat-transfer limitations on magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
As-deposited samples contain microstructural defects and internal stresses that cause greater hysteresis.
Defects and internal stresses in the as-deposited samples degrade their low-field magnetocaloric response.
Annealed samples will have a smaller hysteresis-loop area than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric temperature change under the same low applied field than the as-deposited baseline.
The proposed effects apply during low-applied-field cycling near the relevant magnetic transition temperature.
Applicable cycle frequencies are constrained by intrinsic heat-transfer rates.
The magnitudes of hysteresis reduction and magnetocaloric enhancement may depend on annealing temperature and duration.

Failure of annealing to produce a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and magnetocaloric enhancement, or failure to produce measurable microstructural improvement, is specified as a falsifying result.
